parallel.requirements: Recognized pure Node ESM, .mjs, no npm, no node:crypto cipher APIs, manual argparse parity, Python bytes repr, AES ECB behavior, and /output/test13.mjs delivery. It also introduced a child contract that over-broadened data length to multiples of 16.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent probed the executable, then split work into three child scopes: AES tables/core/ECB, pybytes formatting, and CLI plus entry. Parent retained integration and final verification ownership after AgentSwarm returned.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote lib/aes-tables.mjs, lib/aes-core.mjs, lib/aes-ecb.mjs, lib/pybytes.mjs, lib/cli-args.mjs, and test13.mjs. Parent later edited aes-ecb.mjs and cli-args.mjs to align with pyaes and argparse edge behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact contained /output/test13.mjs plus five files under /output/lib. Parent ran the entry against samples and randomized executable comparisons after consuming child handoffs.
parallel.verification: Verification included FIPS AES vectors, sample cases, syntax checks, parser self-tests, black-box comparisons, data/key length probes, abbreviation and leading-dash argparse checks, and final smoke/sample diffs.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite local checks, the current official evaluator passed only 12 of 108 samples, so remaining failures are not resolved by available trajectory evidence. The visible coordination issue was corrected locally but consumed parent rework.

serial.requirements: Recognized pure ESM, .mjs files, manual CLI parsing, no external dependencies or crypto cipher APIs, AES ECB encryption/decryption, Python bytes repr, and executable-based behavior matching.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned discovery, all module implementation, test13.mjs assembly, black-box comparisons, and final reporting without delegation or subagent handoffs.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote root-level /output/aes.mjs, /output/ecb.mjs, /output/pybytes.mjs, /output/argparse.mjs, and /output/test13.mjs, then wired the entry to those local modules.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integration happened in one workspace by the same actor, with artifact validation listing the five generated root-level files and expected entry test13.mjs present.
serial.verification: The serial run checked executable sample behavior first, then ran four sample comparisons, a FIPS vector, randomized executable comparisons, repr edge cases, and CLI error/help paths.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run also officially failed 96 of 108 samples despite its local checks. Available evidence does not reveal the hidden evaluator cases causing the shared low score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the major prompt requirements but delegated an AES child contract that allowed multiple-of-16 data rather than the source's 16-byte data obligation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received the complete prompt directly and implemented the same broad task as a single actor, including AES, bytes repr, manual CLI parsing, and test13 entry.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both attempted the full port; the meaningful process difference is that parallel transformed part of the task requirement through a child brief while serial kept one local context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into three child-owned scopes for AES, pybytes, and CLI/entry, while the parent retained final integration and test ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had one actor own all discovery, implementation, integration, verification, and final response steps.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced coordination boundaries and handoffs; serial did not have cross-agent ownership boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel supplied explicit module exports and paths in the child briefs, but the AES child received an over-broad data-length behavior requirement and returned that behavior in its handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used direct executable probes and wrote all contracts internally, avoiding a child brief handoff boundary even though it still failed official hidden tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel context transfer created a real rework episode; the serial path had no analogous inter-agent context transfer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced a lib/ hierarchy with AES tables/core/ECB, pybytes, CLI parser, and test13 entry, then patched AES and CLI behavior after integration tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced root-level aes, ecb, pybytes, argparse, and test13 modules in one implementation pass and then tested them locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The final file layouts and repair paths differ, but both delivered executable test13.mjs artifacts and both failed the official suite at the same rate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All three children completed and returned summaries through AgentSwarm; the parent consumed the aggregate and continued with inspection and repairs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to retrieve; the single actor proceeded directly from implementation to verification and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel result lifecycle was complete but included a child-output correction; serial had no join or return lifecycle boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Children wrote separate assigned files in /output/lib and /output/test13.mjs; parent later edited child-created AES and CLI files and validated the final tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor wrote all files itself under /output and assembled imports in test13.mjs without concurrent shared-state writes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared a workspace across actors but kept file scopes separated; the only post-handoff changes were parent repairs, not concurrent write collisions.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran sample diffs, randomized executable comparisons, syntax checks, data/key length probes, argparse abbreviation and leading-dash checks, and final sample smoke tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran executable probes, four sample comparisons, a FIPS vector, randomized comparisons, repr edge cases, and CLI error/help checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on local black-box and smoke checks that missed the hidden official failures; parallel performed extra post-handoff repair validation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed substantially more wall-clock and tokens due to subagents and repair loops but completed before timeout with final checks and response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed much faster with fewer tool calls and no delegation, then closed after its own local verification suite.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The budget profile differs sharply, but neither run timed out and the official completed outcomes are identical failures.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current completed status evaluations report solution_passed false with 12 of 108 samples passed. The parallel run differs procedurally because it delegated component implementation and then repaired child-produced AES and CLI behavior after integration checks; the serial run implemented a different root-level module layout in a single actor. The available pair evidence supports a parallel coordination rework episode but does not prove that episode caused the shared official failure.
parallel_contributors: Delegated AES, pybytes, and CLI/entry work to separate children, then integrated and repaired returned modules.
Corrected the child-produced AES data-length behavior and CLI argparse edge cases after black-box mismatches.
serial_contributors: Kept all implementation and verification in one actor with no child handoff boundaries.
Delivered root-level modules rather than the parallel run's lib/ hierarchy while still producing test13.mjs.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel supported AES-128/192/256 in lib modules and then restricted ECB data to one block; serial described AES-128 and root-level ecb over 16-byte multiples.
Both local test suites emphasized visible samples and random 16-byte cases, while the hidden official suite still failed most cases.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator's per-case failure details are not present in /pair, so the exact hidden failing cases cannot be attributed from allowed evidence.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: both_fail with supported process contrast only; no exclusive root cause for the shared official failure is evidenced

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership existed: the AES, pybytes, and CLI/entry children each received implementation scopes, and the parent later performed integration and repairs.
The parent explicitly owned post-swarm integration and verification after receiving all three child reports, then inspected and edited returned modules.
The CLI/entry child owned /output/test13.mjs and the parent validated the final artifact list; no required entry point was left ownerless.
The parent ran the end-to-end pipeline from delegation through black-box comparisons and final smoke tests, so the implementation-build-test-delivery path had an owner.
The parent did a brief executable probe, but then launched implementation subagents; productive work was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight with an unfinished-work consequence.
The parallel children performed implementation work concurrently rather than only investigation followed by deferred implementation.
No indispensable path was starved: all child scopes returned, and the parent had time to inspect, edit, and rerun black-box checks.
Only three children were launched, the run did not time out, and budget consumption did not prevent final integration or verification.
The AES child had the broadest scope but completed code and checks; its later correction was due to a briefed task-behavior mismatch, not an unfinishable oversized allocation.

The executed AES child was told data length should be a multiple of 16 even though the task source constrained key and data to 16 bytes; the child followed that over-broad brief and the parent later had to repair the child-owned wrapper after executable probing.
candidates.realized_consequence: The child-produced ECB wrapper embodied the over-broad multiple-of-16 data behavior, so the parent had to take over that child-owned module, edit its data-length checks, and rerun integration tests.
candidates.near_match_reason: The exports and import paths were specified up front; the concrete defect was an incorrect task behavior requirement in the AES child brief rather than a missing interop contract.

candidates.reason: The parent supplied explicit exports and import paths for AES, pybytes, CLI parsing, and the entry file; no incompatible independently produced interface remained uncontracted.
No known finding disappeared in transfer; child reports were available to the parent and the later repair came from an incorrect initial child requirement.
The child handoffs were detailed but the parent consumed them, inspected files, and acted on black-box results; no oversized report was left materially unprocessed.
No receiver acted on a superseded child report after a newer workspace state was visible; the parent performed direct edits and post-edit validation.
Children noted the malformed sample hex consistently as a task-brief typo, and no incompatible returned contracts remained unadjudicated.

The parent did not rely only on workflow completion; it ran sample diffs, randomized comparisons, syntax checks, edge-case checks, and final smoke tests before closure. The official failure alone is hidden evaluator evidence, not this pattern.
There was no replacement child or repeated retry without inherited findings; the parent repaired the existing files directly.

The parent did not wait to timeout; it actively inspected results, ran comparisons, edited files, and completed normally.
The children wrote distinct assigned files with an explicit integration contract; no competing cross-file design required unresolved reconciliation.
No two live agents edited the same file concurrently; parent edits occurred after child completion and were part of takeover integration.
The parent edited child-produced source after handoff but did not replace or wholesale rewrite another live agent's non-entry source with an adverse provenance consequence.
The required entry file was created by the CLI child and not overwritten by a concurrent actor; parent edits targeted library/parser behavior.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replacing multiple current outputs or invalidating final-tree provenance.
Although children shared /output, they had separated file scopes and no unstable state or provenance problem is evidenced.
No generated fixture, cache, temporary path, or auxiliary implementation from one actor was consumed by another as a stable reference environment in a contaminating way.
